text:
samir: heads up — noticed a regression in the JS SDK publish we did yesterday. Vercel edge sample app fails to boot: bundler ends up resolving the CJS entry and then crashes on "Cannot use import statement outside a module".

maria: can you paste the exact error / stack? is it only on Vercel Edge or also node apps?

samir: stack trace is small: 
```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:999:30)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1027:10)
```
Only repro so far on the edge sample app + a Next.js middleware build. Node server apps import the CJS build fine.

kevin: sounds like package.json exports map fallback is hitting `./cjs/index.js`. Did we forget the `browser`/`edge` hint or conditional exports for edge runtimes?

samir: I think the conditional exports are present but some bundlers (next, esbuild via vercel) prefer the CJS path unless we expose an explicit `edge` or `import` condition. Current exports snippet in publish: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js"
  }
},
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
```
But the edge build seems to prefer `require` unless we add an `edge` condition.

jamie: yeah, we've had similar with workers runtimes. Two options: add a dedicated `edge` condition in exports, or flip to default `import` (ESM) and provide a `require` condition explicitly for CJS consumers. Flipping default to ESM is breaking though.

leo: adding "edge": "./dist/esm/index.js" usually helps Vercel, but then older bundlers that look for `require` may break. We need to consider telemetry: who is on CJS still?

maria: telemetry: ~18% of installs on our npm metrics are CJS consumers (older LTSs and some backend infra). Many of internal examples and the SDK sample apps are still CJS-based.

kevin: another pain point is typings entry point. Consumers using `import type` sometimes pick the wrong `types` entry when conditional exports are used and no `types` subpath is set. We should publish `./types/index.d.ts` and add an explicit `types` export in exports map: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```
But TS resolver doesn't look at `exports` in some bundlers, so we also need `types` top-level field — which we already have.

samir: root ask: propose we change publish strategy to: default to ESM in exports (so edge-friendly), add `require` condition for CJS, add explicit `edge` condition as alias to ESM to satisfy Vercel esbuild resolution, and add an `./types` subpath export for tsserver. Also update sample apps (edge sample) to import the ESM entry explicitly.

jamie: sounds reasonable. Also add a short CI smoke that builds the Next.js edge sample (via `vercel build` or `next build`) to catch regressions. I can add a GitHub Actions job that runs the edge sample packaging step.

leo: FYI auth/retry mismatch: we found the retry wrapper is only exported on CJS build in previous versions (bad rollup config). If we flip to ESM default we must ensure the retry/auth surface parity is identical between bundles. We should add a quick diff check in the release pipeline: run `node` on both builds to compare exported keys.

maria: +1 on parity check. Also maybe a small note in the changelog for consumers migrating to ESM default so platform teams can opt-in before we switch.

ci-bot: release-check: edge-sample smoke tests queued (workflow: edge-sample-smoke).

kevin: plan of action: 1) change exports map to default to `import` + add `edge` alias, 2) add `./types` export, 3) add parity script in CI (diff exports), 4) run edge sample smoke in release CI, 5) update sample app import docs. I'll open a PR with the export change + CI jobs.

samir: thanks — appreciate quick turnaround. tagging @jamie to help author the CI job and @leo to validate retry/auth export parity.

maria: small follow-up: also check bundler warnings for dual-package consumers — sometimes they bundle both builds and cause duplicate symbols. We should verify the package boundary isn't causing two copies of runtime helpers.

samir: noted. if anyone hits the issue while PR is up ping me and I'll post the temporary workaround (explicit `import { createClient } from 'sdk/dist/esm'`).

kevin: PR -> #4102 (WIP).
